Prophecies and Apparitions

Scene and task

IV.1 · The witches prepare their cauldron.

Use the scene reminder to check the context. Complete the cards or sentences and answer the questions. First checks stay in your record.

Scene reminder

The witches prepare their cauldron. Macbeth arrives demanding answers, even if nature and society are destroyed. An armed head warns him to beware Macduff, Thane of Fife. A bloody child tells him that none of woman born shall harm him. A crowned child holding a tree says he will not be defeated until Great Birnam Wood comes to Dunsinane. The three figures and their messages must be kept distinct.

False Security

Scene and task

IV.1 · Macbeth treats the second and third messages as protection.

Use the scene reminder to check the context. Complete the cards or sentences and answer the questions. First checks stay in your record.

Scene reminder

Macbeth treats the second and third messages as protection. He assumes that everyone is born of woman and that a rooted forest cannot march. However, he still wants to kill Macduff to make assurance double sure. This contradiction shows that reassurance has not removed his fear. The wording states conditions; it does not explain every way those conditions could be fulfilled. Hecate’s warning about dangerous security belongs to III.5 and provides background, not a new speech in IV.1.

Banquo’s Line

Scene and task

IV.1 · Macbeth demands to know whether Banquo’s descendants will reign.

Use the scene reminder to check the context. Complete the cards or sentences and answer the questions. First checks stay in your record.

Scene reminder

Macbeth demands to know whether Banquo’s descendants will reign. Eight kings appear; the last carries a mirror showing further kings, and Banquo’s ghost points to the line as his descendants. This supernatural spectacle renews Macbeth’s fear of a dynasty that is not his own. Banquo does not come back to life, and Fleance is not crowned in this act.

Macbeth’s Decision

Scene and task

IV.1 · After the witches vanish, Lennox reports that Macduff has fled to England.

Use the scene reminder to check the context. Complete the cards or sentences and answer the questions. First checks stay in your record.

Scene reminder

After the witches vanish, Lennox reports that Macduff has fled to England. Macbeth resolves to make the first impulses of his heart the first deeds of his hand. He orders an attack on Fife and the slaughter of Macduff’s wife, children and household. The witches warn him about Macduff; they do not command him to murder the family. This is Macbeth’s own decision, directed against people who cannot threaten his throne militarily.

Macduff’s Family

Scene and task

IV.2 · Lady Macduff criticises her husband for leaving his family exposed.

Use the scene reminder to check the context. Complete the cards or sentences and answer the questions. First checks stay in your record.

Scene reminder

Lady Macduff criticises her husband for leaving his family exposed. Ross defends him cautiously, suggesting wisdom rather than simply cowardice. The son’s witty questions about traitors expose a world in which dishonest people outnumber the honest. A messenger warns the family, but the murderers arrive before they reach safety. The son is stabbed on stage. Lady Macduff flees pursued by the murderers; Ross later reports that she, the children and servants have been killed. The scene exposes the vulnerability of innocent people under tyranny.

Resistance in England

Scene and task

IV.3 · Malcolm fears that Macduff may be Macbeth’s agent.

Use the scene reminder to check the context. Complete the cards or sentences and answer the questions. First checks stay in your record.

Scene reminder

Malcolm fears that Macduff may be Macbeth’s agent. He pretends to be lustful, greedy and without kingly virtues. Macduff initially tries to accommodate individual faults, but rejects a ruler who would destroy Scotland. His despair for the country convinces Malcolm of his integrity. Malcolm retracts the false accusations against himself and offers cooperation. Edward’s healing, reported by a doctor and Malcolm, contrasts with the wounds Macbeth inflicts on Scotland. Ross first describes national suffering and then reveals the family murders. Macduff feels grief and guilt about his absence, but he is not responsible for Macbeth’s crime. He insists that he must also feel it as a man. Malcolm encourages action against Macbeth; English support under Siward is already available. The army is not created solely by Ross’s news.

From Prophecy to Resistance — Timeline

Act IV · Reconstruct the sequence

Move the ten steps using ↑ and ↓ into the order in which the play presents them. Numbers show current positions, not answers. Select Check timeline to review the order; Shuffle steps preserves your first-check record.

Follow the order in which events and reports are presented. The English support is already available before Ross reveals the family murders; do not confuse the presentation order with the date of every off-stage event.

Correct sequence
  1. The consultation: Macbeth demands answers from the witches.
  2. The warning: The armed head names Macduff.
  3. The reassurances: The children speak of birth and Birnam Wood.
  4. The royal line: Eight kings appear with Banquo’s ghost.
  5. The report: Lennox announces Macduff’s flight.
  6. The decision: Macbeth orders the attack on Fife.
  7. The family scene: A warning fails to prevent the attack.
  8. The loyalty test: Malcolm tests Macduff and retracts his claims.
  9. The terrible news: Ross reveals the family murders.
  10. The shared cause: Grief strengthens the resolve to confront Macbeth.

Explain Act IV

Explain how false security becomes tyranny

How does Act IV expose Macbeth’s tyranny and build resistance against it?

Write a connected explanation of about 150–220 words. Include at least two specific events and one short quotation. Connect the apparitions, dynastic fear, the family attack, Malcolm’s test and Macduff’s response.

  1. Write your own explanation first.
  2. Open the bullet-point key and compare all six connections.
  3. Assess each point honestly, revise your writing and update the self-check.
  4. Review the checks, confirm revision and select Complete writing review.

Interpretations need textual support. This self-check is not automatic grading.

Important Quotes from Act IV

Identify, interpret and optionally translate

For each quotation, choose the speaker and then its closest contextual focus. Here “speaker” means the character who says or reports these words in the scene. A thematic focus is an interpretation supported by context, not the only possible association.

Five quotations include an optional German translation: write your own before opening the working translation, then check meaning rather than identical wording. The final relevance note shows how a quotation supports an explanation.

These bonus results do not lower the core revision ratings.
